messages:
marta: quick ask — can someone run an overhead bench comparing streaming + function/tool calls vs non-streaming for our api? p99s in prod look elevated on flows that call 2–3 tools mid-generation :thinking_face:

alex: I can run something on the dedicated pool. what payloads/configs do you want? model, seq len, function schema?

marta: thanks. minimal set: model=gpt-redwood-2-8b, prompt ~120 tokens, max_new_tokens=256, temperature=0.0, streaming=true|false variants. include a function call sequence where the model emits a function call, we synchronously invoke a mock tool (50ms sleep) and then resume streaming. also a structured-output test (JSON schema -> validate).

marta: here's a quick curl example you can use as a starting point:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-2-8b","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"summarize and then call tool"}],"stream":true,"functions":[{"name":"get_price","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"symbol":{"type":"string"}}}}],"max_tokens":256}'
```

alex: perf-bot: queued a run on dc-dedicated-02 (job id 3329) :gear:

perf-bot: benchmark job 3329 started — harness: rt-bench-v3; sample_count=100; warmup=10

jia: what metrics do we want collected? p50/p95/p99 token latency, end-to-end latency, gpu_util, mem, and per-request overhead for the function call (call-time + serialization). also please capture trace with kv-cache hits.

kevin: note CI harness had noisy p99 earlier today due to other tenants on the node. try to pin to an isolated instance or run multiple repeats and median-of-means.

sam: I'll run a structured-output-only variant and collect our json-validate cost separately. also will capture the streaming chunk size distribution (bytes per chunk) — that seems to affect p99.

alex: first quick numbers from job 3329 (streaming + mock-tool 50ms): p50=18ms/token, p95=42ms/token, p99=120ms/token. non-streaming variant: p50=16ms, p95=28ms, p99=78ms. so streaming + tool path adds ~40ms at p99 in this run. uploaded logs and csv -> https://gist.github.com/redwood/perf/3329 (raw csv + charts)

marta: oof. that delta at p99 is too high for some customers. can we profile where the 40ms is? is it serialization, ack flush, or runtime scheduling?

jia: asking for a flamegraph. alex/sam can you capture tokio trace + runtime cpu stacks and a kernel-level perf sample? I suspect batching interaction when we pause for the tool call causes delayed scheduling of the streaming writer.

sam: capturing triton/gpu timelines now. also will run a run with function-call mocked but executed off-net (no 50ms sleep) to isolate the tool latency vs runtime overhead.

alex: added a follow-up run 3331: same config but tool latency=0ms. preliminary: p99 drops to ~90ms. so ~30ms of the 40ms seems from the tool roundtrip itself, remaining ~10ms from stream resumption overhead.

marta: good to know. can we also test with smaller streaming chunk sizes (128 bytes) vs larger (1k) to see flush cost? might be that the stream yields tiny frames after resumption.

perf-bot: job 3331 finished. results attached in gist 3331.

kevin: if resumption cost is ~10ms that's fixable in runtime — maybe consolidate resume path to avoid extra scheduling hop. but confirm with profiler before changing code.

jia: agree. please attach the tokio traces and a short repro script. also create a tiny perf ticket and tag eng-runtime so we can prioritize.

alex: created PR draft with repro and a small instrumentation change to measure resume latency: https://github.com/redwood/rt/pull/1482 (WIP). tagging @marta @jia for review.

marta: thanks. if we can get a reliable <5ms resume we should close this. timeline: try to gather full traces + flamegraphs by Monday. will follow up in this thread. :calendar:

sam: on it — I'll attach GPU traces and the chunk-size experiment results tomorrow.

marta: quick ask for reviewers: if anyone has cycles please skim the PR and the repro script — want eyes before I assign a ticket to onboard the fix. :pray:
